title: Right for the Wrong Reasons? Evaluating Plausibility and Behavioral Change in Explanation-Guided Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.14134v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Explanation-Guided Learning (EGL) promises models that are not only accurate but also rely on task-relevant evidence. However, whether improved agreement between model explanations and human-provided rationales also implies a changed decision strategy remains unclear. We study this tension under controlled synthetic shortcut introduction using a constructed shortcut dataset. Inspired by real-world applications, our benchmark covers shortcuts of different kinds, including localized, background-based, and global cues. This allows us to evaluate whether different EGL objectives produce behavioral changesand explanatory changes. Across these axes, we find that the effects of EGL are strongly objective-specific. Rationale-based data augmentation provides the clearest robustness gains when shortcut evidence can be separated from task-relevant foreground information, reaching average accuracy improvements of up to +4.8 percentage points (pp) to

translated_title: 理由对但原因错？评估解释引导学习中的合理性与行为改变
translated_abstract: 解释引导学习（EGL）承诺构建不仅准确、而且依赖任务相关证据的模型。然而，模型解释与人类提供的理由之间一致性的提高，是否也意味着模型决策策略的改变，这一点仍不清楚。我们通过使用构建的捷径数据集，在受控合成捷径引入的条件下研究这一矛盾。受现实世界应用的启发，我们的基准涵盖不同类型的捷径，包括局部线索、基于背景的线索和全局线索。这使我们能够评估不同的EGL目标是否能产生行为上的改变和解释上的改变。研究发现，EGL的效果在不同目标之间差异很大，具有很强的目标特异性。当捷径证据能够与任务相关的前景信息分离时，基于理由的数据增强提供了最明显的鲁棒性提升，平均准确率提升高达+4.8个百分点。
tldr: 研究表明解释引导学习（EGL）的效果高度依赖具体目标，其中基于理由的数据增强在捷径证据可与任务相关前景信息分离时带来最显著的鲁棒性提升（准确率最高提升4.8个百分点），且模型解释与人类理由的一致性提升并不必然意味着决策策略的真正改变。
